name: Cable Close-Grip Seated Row
summary: A seated compound cable exercise using a close-grip handle to build mid-back thickness, lats, and elbow flexors.

setup: Attach a V-grip (double-D) handle to a low pulley cable station.
Sit on the bench, place your feet against the footrests with knees slightly bent, and grasp the handles with a neutral grip.
Push back with your legs to establish a tall, upright torso with a slight natural arch in the lower back and arms fully extended.
steps: Initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blades and driving your elbows straight back alongside your ribcage.
Pull the handle into your lower abdomen while keeping your chest lifted and torso upright.
Pause momentarily at peak contraction to squeeze your mid-back and lats.
Control the weight back to the starting position under tension, allowing your shoulder blades to protract slightly without rounding your lower back.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you row the handle into your abdomen, and inhale as you return the weight smoothly to full arm extension.
cues: Drive the elbows back, not the hands.
Control the stretch on the way out.

common_faults.fault: Excessive torso swinging and momentum to initiate the row.
common_faults.correction: Keep your torso stationary near vertical and let the arms and back perform the work.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulders upward toward the ears during the pull.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulders depressed and drive your elbows down and back.

common_faults.fault: Fully locking out knees with rounded lumbar spine during the eccentric phase.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a soft knee bend and brace your core to keep a neutral spine.

precautions: Avoid letting the weight stack slam or pulling your lower back into extreme flexion when reaching forward.
